title: Micro-commit lanes: compact cycle funnel and staffing shadow playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: recurring mid-cycle scope churn and surge staffing requests cause unpredictable commitments and cross-team context switching. Goal: introduce a compact, repeatable playbook for mid-cycle micro-commits (micro-commit lanes) that preserves throughput while reducing emergency reallocations. The playbook defines a lightweight funnel for proposals, a staffing shadowing protocol for rapid coverage, automated signals to defer non-critical work, and clear guardrails for scope cuts. This ticket produces the initial operational runbook, tooling inputs (dashboard filters and Slack alerts), and a one-cycle pilot with two squads.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook document published in Confluence with step-by-step funnel and cut matrix
Dashboard panels (Grafana) with automated velocity and outage risk signals configured
Pilot executed across two squads for one cycle with retrospective notes and metrics
Staffing shadow rotation scheduled and no more than one emergency cross-alloc per squad during pilot
A/B evaluation: pilot squads show <=15% higher retained planned scope vs control squads under comparable load
tasks: Draft playbook outline and cut matrix (PM)
Define metric thresholds and Grafana queries (Data/Observability)
Implement Slack alerting channel and webhook for funnel submissions (Eng infra)
Design staffing shadow rota template and on-call handoff doc (People Ops/Eng leads)

Collect pilot telemetry and run retrospective; publish summary to exec stakeholders

decision_log: Trade-off: strict pre-approval stage vs speed. Decision: allow immediate micro-commit lane intake for <3 point tasks with auto-approver (tech-lead) to minimize friction; larger items require quick triage meeting.
Trade-off: shadowing increases short-term headcount pressure. Decision: rotate 1 engineer per squad per week (max 20% capacity) and measure net context-switch cost in pilot.

Cut criteria decision: use composite score (customer impact, effort, regression risk, dependency count). Items scoring <=4 default to deferred; >=7 remain on critical path. Matrix included in runbook.
Automation decision: use existing usage/latency signals first; avoid building new instrumentation for pilot to accelerate rollout. If pilot successful, invest in dedicated scoring service Q3.

rollout_plan: Week 0: finalize runbook and dashboards. Week 1-4: pilot with two squads. Week 5: collect telemetry (velocity, emergency reallocs, planned scope retention), run retrospective, and publish results to exec. If pilot meets acceptance criteria, prepare org-wide 2-cycle rollout plan with templated Slack channels, on-call rotas, and an automated funnel web form. If pilot fails, record failure modes and iterate on thresholds or staffing mix.
